article.title: Running Warm-Up
article.population: People following the NHS Couch to 5K plan; general education
article.context: Walking transition within the source running plan
article.definition: The NHS Couch to 5K plan begins each run with a five-minute walk at a gentle pace.

claims.text: The NHS Couch to 5K plan begins each run with a five-minute walk at a gentle pace.

limitations: This is the source plan’s walking component only. The linked NHS page also discusses stretching; no unsupported stretch sequence is supplied here.
The timer is a source target, not a personal readiness test or proof that pain, illness or injury has resolved.
No heart-rate zone, calorie expenditure or injury-prevention guarantee is inferred.
contraindications: Follow the NHS advice to stop if something does not feel right. If concerned about your health before starting, speak to a healthcare professional.

review.reviewer: Codex source verification and machine validation; personal use; no human review

routine.title: Running Warm-Up

steps.title: Source walking step
steps.intensityCue: Walk gently at a pace comfortable for you before the source running session.
steps.techniqueCue: Follow the linked NHS walking instructions; no additional gait technique is prescribed.
stopSignals: Stop if something does not feel right.

routine.notes: Read-only repository template. Copying creates an independent local routine, not clinical review. Source: https://www.nhs.uk/better-health/get-active/get-running-with-couch-to-5k/couch-to-5k-running-plan/

stepRationales: NHS explicitly supplies a five-minute walking transition; 5 × 60 = 300 seconds. This step has no inferred canonical exercise relationship.
